topics.title: Circuit Analysis and Theorems
topics.syllabus: Node and mesh analysis, superposition, Thevenin's theorem, Norton's theorem, reciprocity.

cards.title: Thevenin and Norton
cards.bodyHtml: Replace everything to the left of a port by one source and one impedance. VthV_{th}Vth​ is the open-circuit voltage; RthR_{th}Rth​ is what you see with independent sources killed — voltage sources shorted, current sources opened.
cards.pitfallHtml: With a dependent source you cannot just kill sources — apply a 1 V test source and find the current, or use Voc/IscV_{oc}/I_{sc}Voc​/Isc​.

formulas.exprHtml: Vth=Voc,IN=Isc,Rth=VocIscV_{th}=V_{oc},\qquad I_{N}=I_{sc},\qquad R_{th}=\frac{V_{oc}}{I_{sc}}Vth​=Voc​,IN​=Isc​,Rth​=Isc​Voc​​
formulas.noteHtml: the ratio form works even with dependent sources

formulas.exprHtml: Rth=RNR_{th}=R_NRth​=RN​
formulas.noteHtml: the two models share the same impedance

cards.title: Maximum power transfer
cards.bodyHtml: Power in the load peaks when the load matches the source. For AC the match is the complex conjugate, which cancels the reactance.

formulas.exprHtml: RL=Rth (DC),ZL=Zth∗ (AC)R_L=R_{th}\ \text{(DC)},\qquad Z_L=Z_{th}^{*}\ \text{(AC)}RL​=Rth​ (DC),ZL​=Zth∗​ (AC)
Pmax=Vth24RthP_{max}=\frac{V_{th}^{2}}{4R_{th}}Pmax​=4Rth​Vth2​​
formulas.noteHtml: at the match, efficiency is only 50%

cards.title: Superposition
cards.bodyHtml: With several independent sources, find the response to each alone and add. Only independent sources are switched off; dependent ones stay active throughout.

formulas.exprHtml: kill: V→short, I→open\text{kill: }V\to\text{short},\ I\to\text{open}kill: V→short, I→open

cards.bodyHtml: ZZZ, YYY, hhh and ABCDABCDABCD describe the same network in different currencies. Convert with a matrix inverse; pick whichever makes the connection type easy — ZZZ adds in series, YYY in parallel, ABCDABCDABCD multiplies in cascade.

cards.title: Star–delta transformation
cards.bodyHtml: Used to unlock bridges that are neither series nor parallel. For three equal elements the ratio is simply 3.

formulas.noteHtml: when all three are equal

cards.title: Node and mesh analysis
cards.bodyHtml: Count first and pick the smaller system: N−1N-1N−1 node equations for NNN nodes, or B−N+1B-N+1B−N+1 mesh equations for BBB branches. Node analysis suits circuits driven by current sources and full of parallel branches; mesh analysis suits voltage sources in series loops.
cards.pitfallHtml: A voltage source between two non-reference nodes has no defined current, so its node equation cannot be written directly — that is exactly when a supernode is required. Grounding one end of it instead removes the problem entirely.

formulas.exprHtml: node equations=N−1,mesh equations=B−N+1\text{node equations}=N-1,\qquad \text{mesh equations}=B-N+1node equations=N−1,mesh equations=B−N+1
formulas.noteHtml: NNN nodes, BBB branches; the second is the number of independent loops

formulas.exprHtml: [G][V]=[I][G][V]=[I][G][V]=[I]
formulas.noteHtml: diagonal = sum of conductances at that node; off-diagonal = −-− the shared conductance

formulas.exprHtml: [R][I]=[V][R][I]=[V][R][I]=[V]
formulas.noteHtml: mesh form; off-diagonal = −-− the shared resistance for consistent loop directions

topics.title: Transient and Steady-State Analysis
topics.syllabus: Time and frequency domain analysis of linear circuits: RL, RC and RLC circuits, solution of network equations using Laplace transform.

cards.title: First-order RL and RC transients
cards.bodyHtml: Every first-order response has the same shape: start value, final value, one time constant. Find those three and write the answer — no differential equation needed.
cards.pitfallHtml: Capacitor voltage and inductor current cannot jump. Everything else can.

formulas.exprHtml: x(t)=x(∞)+[x(0+)−x(∞)]e−t/τx(t)=x(\infty)+\left[x(0^{+})-x(\infty)\right]e^{-t/\tau}x(t)=x(∞)+[x(0+)−x(∞)]e−t/τ
formulas.noteHtml: the universal form

formulas.exprHtml: τ=RCorτ=L/R\tau=RC\quad\text{or}\quad \tau=L/Rτ=RCorτ=L/R
formulas.noteHtml: RRR is the Thevenin resistance seen by CCC or LLL

cards.title: Initial and final conditions
cards.bodyHtml: At t=0+t=0^{+}t=0+ a capacitor holds its previous voltage and an inductor its previous current. After a long time, DC sources leave the capacitor open and the inductor shorted.

formulas.exprHtml: t=0+: vC(0+)=vC(0−),iL(0+)=iL(0−)t=0^{+}:\ v_C(0^{+})=v_C(0^{-}),\quad i_L(0^{+})=i_L(0^{-})t=0+: vC​(0+)=vC​(0−),iL​(0+)=iL​(0−)
formulas.noteHtml: continuity

cards.title: Second-order RLC
cards.bodyHtml: The damping ratio decides the shape. Critically damped is the boundary between overshoot and none, and is the condition GATE most often asks you to impose.

cards.title: Network equations by Laplace transform
cards.bodyHtml: Transform the elements, not the differential equation: RRR stays, LLL becomes sLsLsL, CCC becomes 1/sC1/sC1/sC, and the initial conditions enter as sources in series or parallel with them. The circuit is then solved by ordinary node or mesh analysis in the sss domain.
cards.pitfallHtml: The final value theorem is only valid when every pole of sI(s)sI(s)sI(s) is in the open left half plane. Applying it to an undamped LC circuit returns a number, and that number is meaningless.

formulas.exprHtml: ZL=sL,ZC=1sC,ZR=RZ_L=sL,\qquad Z_C=\frac{1}{sC},\qquad Z_R=RZL​=sL,ZC​=sC1​,ZR​=R

topics.title: Sinusoidal Steady State and Resonance
topics.syllabus: Sinusoidal steady state analysis: phasors, complex power, maximum power transfer.

cards.title: Phasors and impedance
cards.bodyHtml: Replace derivatives with jωj\omegajω and the circuit becomes algebra. The sign of the reactance tells you whether current leads or lags.

Z=R+jXZ=R+jXZ=R+jX
formulas.noteHtml: X>0X>0X>0 inductive, current lags; X<0X<0X<0 capacitive, current leads

cards.bodyHtml: Only the real part is consumed; reactive power sloshes back and forth. Use RMS values throughout.

cards.title: Resonance and Q
cards.bodyHtml: At resonance the reactances cancel and the impedance is purely real. QQQ measures sharpness — and the formula flips between series and parallel.
cards.pitfallHtml: Using the series QQQ on a parallel circuit (or the reverse) is the standard trap.
